supporting_observations.claim: The observed periodic HTTPS tunnel requests from WS-TWEBER-01 were to update.medledger.com, an approved update service. Successful requests are recorded at approximately five-minute intervals from 13:40 through 14:10 UTC.
Endpoint telemetry attributes these connections to C:\Program Files\MediLedger\medledgerupd.exe, matching the approved updater identified in the environment context.

The updater’s repeated destination, roughly five-minute cadence, and similar tunnel byte counts are consistent with the approved MediLedger update-check behavior; a 13:55:32 attempt instead received a proxy 502 gateway error.

known_telemetry_limitations: The proxy records show HTTPS CONNECT tunnel metadata and byte counts, not the encrypted request or response contents (for example, T066-00110 and T066-00270).
The provided records do not include the updater executable’s hash, signature verification, or the contents of any update retrieved.
claims_not_established: The available records do not establish what specific update content, if any, was returned by the successful tunnels.
The records do not independently verify the MediLedger executable’s integrity or signature.
unrelated_findings: Separate review: WS-ESTONE-01 and WS-ARUIZ-01 made inbound TLS connections to WS-TWEBER-01 on port 443, with the workstation’s FQDN shown as the TLS server name. This is outside the alerted outbound activity and is not explained by the provided records; investigate against the remote-administration policy. (T066-00153, T066-00186, T066-00188, T066-00191, T066-00193)
Separate review: WS-RPATEL-01 also attempted a TLS connection to WS-TWEBER-01 on port 443; the connection was reset. This is not the alerted outbound activity. (T066-00247, T066-00249, T066-00250)

Separate review: a Palo Alto GlobalProtect PanGPS process started on WS-TWEBER-01, although the environment context says there is no VPN. The record shows process creation, not that a VPN connection was made. (T066-00277, T066-00278)
